## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The dominant macro narrative entering the week of May 23 is a stagflationary tilt: Brent crude above $103/bbl is reigniting inflationary pressures that are forcing major central banks — led by the Fed — to reconsider the path of monetary policy. U.S. CPI YoY stands at 3.95% as of April 2026, with PPI running at 2.66% MoM, both well above the Fed's 2% target [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL]. The 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to 4.57% and the 2-year sits at 4.08%, producing a positively sloped yield curve that reflects inflation premium rather than growth optimism [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10].

The Federal Reserve's April meeting minutes — released Wednesday — revealed that a majority of participants believe policy firming would be appropriate if inflation persists. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was sworn in on Friday, inheriting an increasingly hawkish committee [Source: https://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-minutes-show-increased-chances-of-interest-rate-hike-e808453b]. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson described current policy as "mildly restrictive" but acknowledged it was "healthy" for markets to price rate hike scenarios [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-20/feds-paulson-says-current-policy-appropriate-healthy-consider-extended]. The effective fed funds rate stands at 3.64%, technically below both CPI and energy-driven inflation pressure, keeping real rates uncomfortably negative [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS].

Nvidia's Q1 results beat Wall Street consensus — analysts had expected EPS of $1.75 and revenue of $78.91 billion — continuing the AI-driven earnings story that has been a key underpinning of equity market resilience [Source: https://apnews.com/article/nvidia-ai-earnings-revenue-955c699a0c91c423edc81b7903b80f85]. The S&P 500 closed at 7,473.47 (+0.37%) on Friday and is tracking toward its longest weekly winning streak since December 2023 [Source: https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-05-22-2026].

The European Commission has cut its 2026 eurozone growth forecast to 0.9% (from 1.2%) and raised inflation projections, citing the energy shock from the Iran war. As a net energy importer, the eurozone faces acute exposure to sustained triple-digit crude prices [Source: https://apnews.com/article/europe-economy-growth-outlook-inflation-4b1eb908b7399c75a7ec8a02a0d3481c]. Meanwhile, 27 countries have approached the World Bank to access crisis funding instruments, reflecting the global financial stress caused by the conflict [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/world-bank-document-shows-27-countries-seeking-ensure-access-crisis-funds-2026-05-23/].

The Bank of Japan is also beginning to signal rate hike intentions, with board member Junko Koeda citing Middle East inflation risks as justification for "raising the policy interest rate at an appropriate pace," adding another dimension to the global monetary tightening cycle [Source: https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/bank-of-japan-policymaker-signals-that-rate-hike-might-be-approaching-6a90860b]. The VIX closed at 16.7, suggesting relatively contained fear despite elevated macro risks, though this may reflect market adaptation to sustained geopolitical uncertainty rather than genuine complacency [Source: Yahoo Finance (^VIX)].
